title: Dynamic batch-slot experiment and QSA gap analysis for per-vector pricing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: validate a dynamic batch-slot pricing model that reduces per-vector unit cost for high-throughput customers while preserving latency SLOs and rerank quality. This ticket covers the product spec, experiment design, QSA pre-check for enterprise contract language, and the rollout gating criteria. We want to capture trade-offs (latency vs unit cost), required runtime changes, and the contractual ask for batch-discount optics in QSA/QSA addenda.
background: Current per-vector proposals assume static slab discounts or fixed batch-credit bundles. Sales feedback indicates customers want discounts that reflect real batch behavior (bursty vs steady) and a clear conversion between 'batch slots' and per-vector units. Engineering flagged kernel-level constraints for very large batch sizes and potential KV-cache hit regressions. Security asked for contract language clarity around retained request metadata for billing reconciliation.
proposal: Introduce a dynamic batch-slot meter: customers purchase 'batch slots' and receive a variable per-vector rate that scales with observed average batch occupancy over a 30-day rolling window. Experiment with two variants: (A) aggressive discount where slot occupancy > 70% yields 25% per-vector discount, (B) conservative discount with occupancy > 85% yields 15% discount. Provide an opt-in pilot with clear guardrails: latency capped to 99th percentile SLO of 600ms on CPU-backed models and automatic fallback to standard per-vector pricing if SLOs are violated for more than 6 hours in a day.
experiment_design: Cohorts: 50 pilot customers split across control (no change), Variant A (aggressive), Variant B (conservative). Duration: 6 weeks with 2-week ramp, 4-week measurement. Metrics windows: daily token counts, batch occupancy distribution, per-embedding cost, P50/P95/P99 latency, rerank NDCG@10 / mean reciprocal rank on canonical evaluation set, error rate. Sample size target: customers with >= 50k vectors/day to ensure statistical power. Data collection: ingest billing signals + runtime telemetry (batch occupancy histograms) into pricing-experiments dataset. Canary behavior: if latency regressions correlate with occupancy > 70% and increase error rate, immediately pause discounts for affected customers and open incident for ENG routing tuning.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal sandbox test with synthetic load and billing emulation (2 weeks). Phase 1: closed pilot with 50 customers (6 weeks experiment). Phase 2: evaluate results and prepare pricing catalog entry + contract language. Phase 3: 8-week ramp to self-serve if KPIs meet pass criteria. Rollout gates: no more than 0.5% customers experience >10% latency degradation; billing reconciliation mismatches <0.1% over 30 days; security sign-off on QSA addendum language.
qsa_notes: Initial QSA review surfaced three gaps: (1) audit trail for batch-slot usage needs explicit log retention and export format for customer audits; (2) data residency implications when batch aggregation occurs across regions; (3) billing reconciliation process and sample reports required for SOC2/enterprise audits. Action items: draft QSA addendum language, add fields to billing export CSV and to audit logs, propose tenant-level config to pin region for batch accounting.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Telemetry pipeline emits daily batch occupancy histograms and integrates with pricing experiments dataset. 2) Billing export includes batch_slots_consumed and effective_per_vector_price fields. 3) Pilot runs for 4 full measurement weeks with KPIs meeting pass gates. 4) QSA addendum text approved by Security and Legal.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large batch discounts could incentivize customers to rework traffic patterns causing latency regressions. Mitigation: automatic fallback and per-customer performance guardrails.
Risk: Billing reconciliation mismatches due to aggregation windows. Mitigation: deterministic windowing and sample reconciliation reports to customers.
Risk: Enterprise QSA requires additional logging and residency constraints. Mitigation: provide tenant pinning and expanded audit export.
Risk: Model quality drift for reranking if batching affects KV cache. Mitigation: include quality eval hooks and daily NDCG checks; immediate rollback if >0.5% regression observed.
